title: Arjuna's austerities
hook: a boar charges, two arrows strike it at once, and a mountain hunter says it was his
carry: one breath before deciding who they are

segments.voice: Yesterday Arjuna's austerities burned so hot the sages went to Shiva, and Shiva said: I know what he wants. Your line was keep discipline without announcing it. Did you keep a small discipline quietly? Day seven hundred eighty-four.

Crashing through the trees, a boar. It's huge, and it's coming straight at Arjuna. The story tells us it's no ordinary animal: a demon named Muka has taken this shape to kill the man at prayer. Thin from fasting, Arjuna still moves fast. He grabs his bow, nocks an arrow and draws. And at that very moment, someone else is drawing too. A hunter has stepped out of the forest, a Kirata, one of the mountain people, with a woman at his side and a crowd behind him. Two archers. One boar. Today, the hunter.
screen: `A BOAR CRASHES THROUGH THE TREES.` → `ARJUNA DRAWS HIS BOW.` → `SO DOES A HUNTER.`

segments.voice: The listener already knows something Arjuna doesn't. The hunter is Shiva. He's come down the mountain in disguise, and the woman beside him is his consort Uma, also disguised. Shiva told the sages, I know what he wants. Now he's come to see what Arjuna is made of. Stop, the hunter calls. I aimed at that boar first. Arjuna ignores him and shoots. So does the hunter. Both arrows strike at the same instant, and the boar falls dead, in its own demon shape again. And Arjuna is furious. Who are you, he demands, roaming this empty forest with women around you? Why did you shoot the game I had already marked? That breaks the rules of the hunt. I'll take your life for it. The hunter isn't impressed. This forest is our home, he says, more or less. I claimed that boar first. And if you think you're strong, shoot. This is the turn the whole week has been walking toward. In the forest, the Pandavas argued about anger and patience, about might and keeping their word. On the mountain, Arjuna held onto his purpose, and burned with tapas until the sages complained. And now, after all that discipline, the first person he meets makes him angry in seconds. The text doesn't hide it. Arjuna's austerities have made him strong. They haven't yet made him humble. And he's about to pick a fight with the very god he came to find.
screen: `THE HUNTER IS SHIVA IN DISGUISE.` · `TWO ARROWS, ONE BOAR.` · `ARJUNA: YOU BROKE THE RULES.` · then, large: `STRONG, BUT NOT YET HUMBLE.`

segments.voice: Let the body settle, and the breath slow. Think back over this week: the forest, the arguments, the waiting, the mountain. Now bring to mind a moment, maybe recent, when someone stepped into your way and you flared up. Breathe in, and see that person again. Breathe out, and wonder, just for a moment: what if they weren't who I thought they were? You don't have to excuse anything. Just leave that question open. If you pray, you can bring that moment into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Arjuna's austerities. They've made him strong enough to face a demon boar, and quick enough to pick a fight with a hunter who is Shiva.
Your line: one breath before deciding who they are. Today, when someone gets in your way, give them one breath before you decide who they are. Day seven hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: The meeting of Arjuna and Shiva as a hunter is retold in Hindu storytelling, poetry and temple art, and Shiva in the guise of a Kirata is honored as a form of the god.

original.note: Sanskrit kirāta: a mountain hunter; Shiva's disguise in this story.

trapdoor: what you thought: a quarrel between two hunters over a boar.
what it means: the hunter is Shiva, come in disguise to meet the man doing austerities for him.
what a scholar hears: the god Arjuna has worked so hard to reach arrives as someone easy to dismiss.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Kairata Parva (Shiva comes as a Kirata with Uma; the danava Muka as a boar; Arjuna and the Kirata shoot together; the quarrel)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm the demon's name (Muka/Mooka) and that he takes boar form to kill Arjuna.
Confirm that Uma accompanies Shiva in disguise, with a host of attendants and women, and that both arrows strike simultaneously.
Confirm Arjuna's words (rebuking the Kirata for shooting game he had aimed at, contrary to the rules of hunting) and the Kirata's reply (that he aimed first, that the forest is his people's home).
Day 784 is a week end; hook and teach look back over days 778-783.
